title: F1: Extract shared JSON envelope crate from dont and adopt suite-wide
description:
Source: CLI consistency audit F1 (🔴) — the "single biggest AIX defect in the suite"

**Problem:** No shared JSON envelope exists across the suite, despite tools being designed to compose. Four different incompatible JSON shapes exist for the same "give me status/health report" family of commands. dont has the canonical envelope (ok, envelope_version, cli_version, envelope_kind, data, warnings, hints, meta) but it is not extracted as a shared crate.

**Expected:** Extract dont's JSON envelope struct/serializer into a shared crate (e.g. "charly-vibes-envelope" or similar) that all tools can depend on. Every --json-capable command in every tool must wrap its payload in this shared envelope.

**Reference implementation:** dont/src/envelope.rs — Envelope, EnvelopeKind, ErrorResult structs.

**Parent of (child adoption issues needed):**
- wai: adopt shared envelope crate, replace bare domain object output
- pretender: adopt shared envelope crate, replace bare JSON array output
- espectacular: adopt shared envelope crate, replace "findings" key vocabulary
- testaruda: adopt shared envelope crate

**Classification:** HITL (architectural decision, needs human review).

**Verification:** All five tools emitting --json should produce output with the same top-level keys (ok, envelope_version, cli_version, data, etc.).
design:
## Crate Architecture

Extract `dont/src/envelope.rs` into a shared crate called `charly-vibes-envelope` (or similar).

### Design Decisions

1. **Distribution:** git dependency from github.com/charly-vibes/envelope (no crates.io publish until the interface stabilizes). Add to Cargo.toml as:
   ```
   charly-vibes-envelope = { git = "https://github.com/charly-vibes/envelope" }
   ```

2. **Interface:** a concrete `Envelope` struct (not a trait) with generics for the `data` field:
   ```rust
   pub struct Envelope<T: Serialize> {
       pub ok: bool,
       pub envelope_version: String,
       pub cli_version: String,
       pub envelope_kind: EnvelopeKind,
       pub data: T,
       pub warnings: Vec<Warning>,
       pub hints: Vec<HintEntry>,
       pub meta: Meta,
   }
   ```

3. **EnvelopeKind:** string enum (Version, Status, Error, Result, etc.)

4. **Adoption order:**
   - Phase 1: Extract crate from dont, publish to charly-vibes/envelope repo
   - Phase 2: Replace dont internal envelope with crate re-export (no-op, verifies API)
   - Phase 3: Adopt in wai, pretender, espectacular, testaruda (one PR each, independently)

5. **Non-goals:** color/formatting helpers, transport logic, CLI flag parsing. Pure serialization only.

title: F23: dont — allow-list events.jsonl in .gitignore (mirror beads !.beads/issues.jsonl pattern)
description:
Source: CLI consistency audit F23

Problem: dont's own claims ledger (events.jsonl) is gitignored by default. The .gitignore written by "dont init" says ".dont/" which hides the entire state directory including events.jsonl. The format was explicitly designed to be append-only/line-based so it survives git merges, yet it is excluded from sharing by default. The beads .gitignore pattern already solves this: ".beads/*" + "!.beads/issues.jsonl".

Expected: Change the generated .gitignore from ".dont/" to ".dont/*" + "!.dont/events.jsonl" (mirror beads pattern). Update docs/enforcement.md to state that events.jsonl is meant to be shared.

Files: dont/.gitignore — hand-edited allow-list currently omits events.jsonl. Source template used by "dont init" — change the .gitignore template.

Verification: "grep 'events.jsonl' dont/.gitignore" should match. "dont init" in a fresh repo should produce a .gitignore that allow-lists events.jsonl.

title: [F2] apply_transition Kleisli helper — collapse 12 duplicated pipelines
description: main.rs lines 3017, 3081, 3221, 3289, 3348, 3447, 3506, 3643, 3725, 3794, 3853 each re-implement the same 7-step pipeline: fetch → lift → transition → marshal-back → append-event → re-fetch → emit. Six transitions × {claim, term} = 12 instantiations of the identical shape.
design:
After F1 (single Status) and F3 (EntityId), introduce:

fn apply_transition<E: Entity>(
    store: &mut Store,
    id: E::Id,
    transition: fn(Status) -> Result<Status, TransitionError>,
    event_kind: EventKind,
) -> Result<E, CliError>

Each of the 12 call sites collapses to a one-liner. Transitions are already model::* functions of shape Status → Result<Status, TransitionError> — true Kleisli arrows.

TDD:
- RED: integration tests for each of the 6 transitions on each entity must already exist; if not, add minimal coverage first
- GREEN: introduce helper, migrate one call site at a time
- REFACTOR: factor common entity trait if needed; otherwise duplicate-for-now is fine
acceptance_criteria: One apply_transition helper. The 12 call sites are each ≤5 LOC. All existing transition tests pass. cargo clippy clean.
notes:
Session 2026-05-15 paused F2 before starting. Verified 12 sites map to these
append_*_status_change call lines: 3019 3083 3202 3289 3348 3447 3506 3624
3707 3794 3853 4581 (last is part of `ground` composition).

Recommended approach (refined after F1+F3 landed):
- Extract two parallel helpers: apply_claim_transition / apply_term_transition.
  Both take (project, id, transition: FnOnce(Status) -> Result<Status, _>,
  event_kind, note: Option<String>, evidence: Vec<Value>, remediation).
- Per-site variations to handle: (a) note presence, (b) evidence vector,
  (c) success_with_tx vs success at L2854, (d) ground composition at L4581
  which chains two transitions, (e) hints in some emit_*_view calls.
- A single generic helper over an Entity trait is possible but probably
  overkill for two kinds — duplicate-for-now is acceptable per ticket design.

Migrate one transition cluster (claim+term pair) at a time; cargo test after
each. Estimated 12 sites × ~6 LOC vs current 60-100 LOC each — ~700 LOC
reduction in main.rs.

title: [F4] Rules catalog — collapse triple-dispatch table to data
description: src/rules/mod.rs has three independent match name tables: list (line 17), explain (line 29), evaluate_shipped (line 120). Drift is currently caught only by runtime tests at lines 397-426 — a Don't-Repeat-Yourself violation guarded by runtime, not types.
design:
Define struct ShippedRule { name: &'static str, check: fn(&Claim)->RuleResult, explanation: &'static str } and a const RULES: &[ShippedRule]. Derive list/explain/evaluate_shipped from iterating the slice.

TDD:

- GREEN: introduce catalog and reimplement the three fns over it
- REFACTOR: drift tests become trivial or are removed (they were structural duplication detectors)
acceptance_criteria: One source of rule metadata. list, explain, evaluate_shipped all derive from a single RULES slice. cargo test passes. The drift tests at 397-426 either pass trivially or can be deleted as redundant.

title: [EPIC] Composability refactor — collapse parallel types and duplicated pipelines
description: Eliminate composability friction identified in 2026-05-15 composability-diagnostician audit. title: TDD: prime exits non-zero when doubted claims exist
description:
## Why this issue exists

dont prime already computes a blocking[] array of doubted claims but always exits 0. The CI gate is toothless until this is fixed — every downstream step depends on this contract.

## What needs to be done

TDD cycle:
1. Write failing test: assert that dont prime returns exit code 1 when at least one claim is in doubted status
2. Fix: in Command::Prime (~line 3546 of src/main.rs), after emit_json(&env), add: if !blocking.is_empty() { process::exit(1) }
3. Verify test passes; run full suite

Gate contract (must be encoded in test): prime exits 1 iff any claim is doubted. Unverified claims do not cause non-zero exit in permissive mode.
notes: Test in tests/integration/ using assert_cmd (or equivalent). Fixture: run 'dont conclude sentinel-claim' then 'dont doubt <id>' via the binary to create a doubted claim. Assert binary exit code is 1. Also assert exit code 0 when no doubted claims exist.
close_reason: TDD fix landed in commit 29a5211: prime now exits 1 when blocking[] is non-empty. Two integration tests added, existing prime_blocking test updated.

title: Bug: verified claim allowed to depend on unverified term
description:
When a claim is created with --depends-on term:ID where the term is unverified, dont conclude correctly warns 'verification blocked until resolved'. However, dont dismiss then succeeds and sets the claim to verified status anyway without checking the dependency.

Spec ref: dont-status-lifecycle §"Persisted status and derived assessment are distinct" — the invariant listed in dont prime: 'Verified entities must not depend on unresolved terms' is not enforced at dismiss time.

Note: This bug is the symptom; dont-711 (unresolved-terms rule, strict by default) is the planned enforcement mechanism, which in turn depends on dont-8cs (Cozo rule engine). Once dont-711 lands, dont dismiss should fire the unresolved-terms rule as a refusal before committing the status change. This issue can be closed when dont-711 is verified to block dismiss on claims with unresolved term dependencies.

Done when:
- dont dismiss claim:ID -e uri on a claim that --depends-on an unverified term exits 1 with the unresolved-terms rule firing as a structured refusal
- dont dismiss succeeds only after all depended-on terms are verified
- cargo test rules::unresolved_terms_blocks_dismiss passes (see dont-711)

title: Bug: duplicate CURIEs allowed when redefining a term
description:
Running dont define WB:P001 twice creates two separate term records with the same CURIE. There is no uniqueness constraint on CURIEs. The second call silently creates a duplicate instead of erroring or updating. This makes it impossible to look up a term by CURIE unambiguously, and causes integrity issues when rules or depends-on references resolve by CURIE.

Spec ref: dont-data-model §"Entity structure" — CURIEs are used as lookup keys in dependency resolution and rules. The dont-glossary spec likely defines CURIE uniqueness; check §"coined term" or §"CURIE" requirements there. If absent, this is both a bug fix and a spec gap.

Done when:
- dont define WB:P001 ... a second time exits 1 with code 'curie-conflict' and a remediation suggesting dont show or dont define with a different CURIE
- The existing term with WB:P001 is unchanged
- cargo test data_model::curie_uniqueness passes

title: Bug: trust/dismiss on terms gives internal error
description:
Running dont trust term:ID --reason '...' or dont dismiss term:ID -e '...' returns an internal error: 'claim term:ID has no statement' with exit code 4. The error message leaks an internal implementation detail (terms being dispatched through the claim handler) and points to dont doctor which does not exist (see dont-736).

Spec ref: dont-status-lifecycle §"Shared persisted status lattice" — the lattice is shared for claims and terms; both SHOULD support trust and dismiss transitions.

Root cause hypothesis: the trust/dismiss command handler queries only the claim table rather than the entity table, so term:ID lookups fail the claim-not-found check and hit a fallback internal error path.

Done when:
- dont trust term:ID --reason 'x' exits 0 and sets term status to doubted, OR exits 1 with code 'not-applicable' if terms intentionally cannot be doubted (requires spec clarification)
- dont dismiss term:ID -e 'uri' exits 0 and sets term status to verified, OR exits 1 with code 'not-applicable'
- No envelope with code 'internal' is emitted for trust/dismiss on a valid term:ID
- cargo test lifecycle::trust_term and lifecycle::dismiss_term pass

title: feat: add `dont check --ungrounded` command for CI/pre-push gate integration
description:
## Why
`dont` has no first-class command that exits non-zero when ungrounded claims exist. Without this, wiring `dont` into a pre-push hook or CI pipeline requires fragile scripting against `dont list` or `dont status` output. Every project that doesn't wire `dont` into a gate will see it decay to zero use (observed in cositos — see dont-pfn3).

## What to build
Add a `dont check --ungrounded` subcommand (exact name TBD — `dont gate`, `dont check`, or `dont verify` are also candidates) that:
- Exits 0 when all claims in the ledger are verified, locked, or ignored.
- Exits non-zero when any claim is in an ungrounded/unverified state.
- Prints a summary of ungrounded claims (human and `--json` modes).
- Is safe to run read-only (no side effects, no state mutations).

## Files
- `src/main.rs` (new subcommand routing)
- `src/commands/check.rs` (or similar)
- Tests under `tests/`
- `dont --help` output

## Acceptance
`dont check --ungrounded` exits 1 when the ledger contains at least one claim in an ungrounded state.
`dont check --ungrounded` exits 0 when all claims are verified, locked, or ignored.
`dont check --ungrounded --json` emits a valid JSON summary.
The command is documented in AGENTS.md alongside the hook snippet (see dont-pfn3).

## Related
- dont-pfn3 (gate docs — companion ticket; documents the hook snippet using this command)
- dont-tqqb (F1: external evidence — gate is only fully effective once this lands)

## Finding
From cositos dogfooding evaluation (sandbox/charly-vibes-tools/dev-tooling-evaluation.md §F20).

1. F1 (external evidence blocked) made grounding painful on first contact.
2. Unlike `pretender` and `ah`, `dont` was never added to the commit/CI gate — nothing broke when it went unused.
3. The two tools that survived did so *exactly because* a gate failed without them.

## Scope (this ticket: docs only)
Add canonical gate integration documentation to AGENTS.md and README:
- A hook snippet showing how to wire `dont` into a pre-push or CI gate.
- A note on which `dont` command should be used as the gate check (e.g. `dont status --fail-on-ungrounded` or similar existing command).
- A brief rationale in AGENTS.md explaining *why* a gate matters for adoption.

This ticket does NOT include implementing a new CLI command — that is tracked separately.

- `.dont/AGENTS.md` (managed block)
- `README.md` (quickstart or workflow section)

## Acceptance
AGENTS.md and README each contain a gate integration section with a copy-pasteable hook snippet. Running the documented command in a repo with ungrounded claims exits non-zero. No new Rust code required to close this ticket.

title: [bug] F23: --evidence flag only accepts URLs; local file path silently belongs to --file instead
description:
## Finding
From cositos dogfooding evaluation (sandbox/charly-vibes-tools/dev-tooling-evaluation.md §F23).

In a code repository the most common evidence is a repo file. The natural first attempt:

```
dont flag claim:… --evidence examples/benchmarks/benchlib.py
→ error: malformed evidence locator "…": must be an http:// or https:// URI
```

The repo-relative path form lives under the separate `--file` flag, which is undiscoverable from the obvious flag name. `--evidence` accepts only URLs.

## Impact
Every agent and new user first tries `--evidence path/to/file.py` for the most common case and gets a confusing, unhelpful error. The split between `--evidence` (URL) and `--file` (path) is invisible from the flag names alone.

## Suggested fix
Either let `--evidence` accept a repo-relative path (routing it to the same locator as `--file`), or rename the URL flag to `--evidence-url` so the split is self-evident. Also update llm.txt / AGENTS.md to document the distinction explicitly.
acceptance_criteria:
`dont flag claim:<id> --evidence path/to/file.py` succeeds (same outcome as `--file path/to/file.py`).
The existing `--evidence https://…` URL form is unaffected.
`dont flag --help` and llm.txt/AGENTS.md document both the path and URL forms under the same conceptual flag.
notes: Preferred fix: extend --evidence to also accept repo-relative paths, routing them to the same locator as --file (additive, non-breaking). Renaming to --evidence-url is an acceptable alternative only if confirmed that no downstream consumers depend on the current --evidence flag name.

title: [bug] F21: dont flag --file rejects evidence files with unstaged edits — forces commit-before-ground
description:
## Finding
From cositos dogfooding evaluation (sandbox/charly-vibes-tools/dev-tooling-evaluation.md §F21).

`dont flag <claim-id> --file <path>` fails when the evidence file has unstaged modifications:

```
dont flag claim:… --file examples/benchmarks/benchlib.py
→ error: file has unstaged modifications; SHA would not match current content
```

Verified live: dirtying a tracked file made the flag fail; after `git checkout --` (clean) the identical command succeeded.

## Impact
You cannot ground a finding against evidence you are actively editing — you must `git commit` the file first, which inverts the natural loop (findings are usually grounded *while* being written up). Combined with F3 (wai artifacts uncommitted) this materially discourages grounding.

## Suggested fix
Hash the working-tree (or staged) content instead of requiring a clean tree, or add an `--allow-dirty` escape hatch.

## Related
- dont-tcy0 (F3: staged-but-uncommitted files)
- dont-lpk (closed — captured provenance requirement; this is the dirty-file sibling)
acceptance_criteria:
`dont flag <claim-id> --file <path>` succeeds against a tracked file that has unstaged (working-tree dirty) modifications.
Existing behaviour for clean (committed) files is unchanged.
The error "file has unstaged modifications; SHA would not match current content" no longer fires for the dirty-but-tracked case (or is downgraded to a warning if provenance capture is still desired).
notes: Likely change site: wherever the file-hash / git provenance check runs before attaching evidence (possibly src/evidence.rs or equivalent). The fix should hash the working-tree content rather than requiring a clean tree, or add an --allow-dirty flag.

title: F1: allow evidence from outside the project root (external repos, vendored paths, URL+commit)
description:
## Parent
Evaluation report: ~/para/projects/astra-zeneca/dev/sandbox/charly-vibes-tools/dev-tooling-evaluation.md §F1

## What to build

`dont ground` currently rejects any `--file` path that escapes the project root:

```
dont ground "…" --file ../anywidget/anywidget/_util.py
→ error: evidence locator path is invalid: path escapes project root
```

For any project that references sibling repos (forks, upstream sources, vendored copies), this makes the core grounding workflow entirely unusable.

## Decision required (HITL)

Choose one or more of the following mechanisms — record the decision as an ADR before implementing:

| Option | Description | Trade-offs |
|--------|-------------|------------|
| **A — Allow-list of external roots** | A workspace-level config key listing allowed parent directories | Explicit, auditable; requires config plumbing |
| **B — Vendored-path escape hatch** | A `--allow-external` flag that bypasses the root check for a single call | Simple; less auditable |
| **C — URL + commit-pinned locators** | Support `--url <github-permalink>` as evidence so the source never needs to live on disk | Best for reproducibility; higher implementation cost |

## Files / Systems
- `src/` — evidence locator path-resolution module
- Locator schema (wherever file-locator path validation lives)
- `llm.txt` / docs — update to document the chosen mechanism

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Decision recorded (ADR or accepted option in this issue)
- [ ] `dont ground "claim" --file ../sibling-repo/file.rs --lines 1-50` succeeds with the chosen mechanism
- [ ] Evidence stored with sufficient provenance to be reproducible
- [ ] Error message for paths outside the root (without the escape) is helpful
- [ ] Tests cover the new path and the existing in-repo path
acceptance_criteria: dont ground accepts a file path outside the project root via the chosen mechanism; provenance is stored; existing in-repo path behaviour is unchanged
notes: Decision: Option C (URL + commit-pinned locators) implemented. Added --url flag to ground, flag, and dismiss commands. New structured evidence kind 'url-permalink' with fields: url, line_start, line_end, anchor, excerpt. Stored as structured JSON locator (like repo-file), not as plain URI string. Conflicts with --file. Tested with 10 new integration tests.

title: Explore feedback loop: log rejected-claim patterns to inform future research
description:
When dont flags an ungrounded claim, the rejection pattern (topic area, evidence type attempted, grounding failure mode) is lost after the session ends. This ticket explores how to capture and aggregate these signals so they can inform future research phases.

## Deliverable

A design document at `dont/docs/feedback-loop-design.md` answering the questions below, reviewed and approved. Followed by an implementation ticket.

## Starting points

- `src/rules/ungrounded.rs:10-28` — ungrounded claim rule firing logic
- `src/main.rs:2331-2358` — strict mode rejection (unresolved term refs)
- `src/envelope.rs:72-105` — ErrorResult struct encapsulating rejections
- `src/main.rs:441-471` — error emission functions (JSON envelope output)
- `src/rules/mod.rs:71-100` — rule severity definitions (strict vs warn)

## Questions to answer

- What structured format should rejected-claim logs use?
- Where should aggregated patterns be stored? (local db, git-tracked file, external)
- How should wai consume this signal — push (dont notifies) or pull (wai queries)?
- What's the minimal viable feedback: just a counter per category, or full claim traces?

## Integration points

- wai research phase: auto-suggest gaps based on historically rejected claim patterns
- openspec constraints: recurring rejection categories could become spec-level validation rules
- espectacular drift: downstream consumer of rejection signals (see espectacular tracer-bullet ticket)

## Sequencing

This is a generalization ticket. Start after the espectacular tracer-bullet proves the end-to-end feedback loop with one concrete signal.

description:

**Epic**: dont-4k5

**Risk if poor**: When the shape of a type or setup requirement changes, every duplicated fixture must be updated independently. Missed updates cause inconsistent test environments and subtle bugs that only surface in some test files.

**Risk if poor**: Failing tests give no diagnostic signal — the developer must read and reverse-engineer the test to understand what broke. Test suite is not self-documenting and becomes harder to maintain over time.
**How to audit**: List all test function names and flag any that: contain generic words only (test, check, basic, simple, it), are numbered, or omit the behavior/condition being verified. Good names follow the pattern: test_<unit>_<scenario>_<expected_result>.

**Risk if poor**: Error handling code is untested and likely broken. The CLI may panic, produce corrupt output, or give misleading error messages in production failure scenarios that were never exercised.
**How to audit**: For each test file, check whether the corresponding production code has error return paths or conditional error handling. Flag any file where tests only call functions with valid inputs and never inject failures or assert on error values.

title: [TEST-QUALITY] Audit test isolation failures in existing tests

**Epic**: dont-4k5

**Risk if poor**: Flaky test suites that fail intermittently depending on run order, parallel execution, or leftover state from previous runs. Makes CI unreliable and hides real bugs behind noise.
**How to audit**: Look for global variables mutated across tests, temp files written without cleanup (missing defer/teardown), tests that only pass when run after a specific other test, and any use of shared singletons or process-level state.

title: [TEST-QUALITY] Audit implementation coupling in existing tests
description:
**Audit Area**: test-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to audit**: Tests that call private or internal functions directly rather than going through the public API surface, making them break on refactors that don't change observable behavior.
**Risk if poor**: Refactoring becomes expensive and risky — tests fail even when behavior is correct, creating noise that masks real failures. Discourages healthy internal restructuring.
**How to audit**: Scan test files for direct calls to unexported/private functions, internal module paths, or bypassing CLI entry points. Flag tests that would need updating after a purely internal rename.

title: [TEST-QUALITY] Audit brittle assertion patterns in existing tests
description:
**Audit Area**: test-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to audit**: Tests that assert on string output format rather than semantic meaning — e.g. checking raw stdout contains a literal string like 'Expected claim' instead of inspecting structured data or return values.
**Risk if poor**: Tests break on cosmetic output changes (rewording, reformatting) while missing real behavioral regressions. False negatives on actual bugs.
**How to audit**: Grep test files for .contains(), string equality on output buffers, and snapshot-style assertions. Flag any test that would fail if a UI string was reworded but behavior stayed identical.

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Claim structure rule edge cases: nested/malformed claims handled
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: The claim structure rule is the parser-facing layer. If it panics or produces wrong results on malformed or deeply nested claim inputs, users get crashes or false-clean reports on structurally invalid files.
**What to check**: Find the claim structure rule in src/rules/. Test it against: (1) an empty claim body, (2) a claim with only whitespace, (3) claims nested 10 levels deep, (4) a claim with a missing required field, (5) a claim with duplicate field keys, (6) a claim referencing a non-existent parent, (7) a claim with a Unicode identifier. For each case, verify the rule either passes or returns a structured Err — never panics. Verify error messages identify the claim and the structural violation.
**Pass criteria**: All 7 edge-case inputs produce either a valid pass or a structured error with claim identifier and violation type; no panics or stack overflows; deeply nested claims do not cause quadratic slowdowns (check with a 100-level nest).
**Fail criteria**: Any input causes a panic, unwrap failure, or stack overflow; malformed claims produce Ok(()) silently; error messages lack claim identifier; 100-level nesting takes more than 1 second.
close_reason: Audit complete: rule_claim_structure handles all edge cases correctly. 5 tests added.

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Large claim graph — performance degrades gracefully not catastrophically
description:
**Audit Area**: robustness — large claim graph performance

**What to test**: Performance degrades gracefully (linear, not exponential) as claim count grows. The specific threshold is 1000 claims for read operations.

**Pass criteria**:
- Any read operation (`dont list`, `dont show`, `dont why`) on a 1000-claim project completes in < 5 seconds on typical developer hardware
- No panic, no hang, no OOM under 1000 claims
- Degradation beyond 1000 claims is acceptable if it is linear — exponential growth is a hard failure

**Test approach**: Create a project with 1000 claims via a script (loop calling `dont assert` or by injecting events directly into the store). Time `dont list`, `dont show <id>`, and `dont why <id>` against the populated store. Record wall-clock time and confirm it stays under the 5-second threshold.

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Missing required config fields — clear error with fix instructions
description:
**Audit Area**: error-handling-robustness
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Failure mode**: A required field in the project config (e.g. project name, storage backend, output format) is absent from the TOML file
**Expected behavior**: Error message names the missing field, explains what it controls, shows the valid value range or example, and points to the config file path; does not fall back to an undocumented default
**Current risk**: serde default attributes may silently substitute empty strings or zero values, masking the misconfiguration until a downstream operation fails with an unrelated error

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Dangling definition detection: correctly identifies all orphan patterns
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: A dangling definition — a term defined but never referenced, or referenced but never defined — is a primary epistemic integrity violation. If the detector has false negatives, users believe their definitions are clean when they are not.
**What to check**: Identify the rule implementing dangling definition detection in src/rules/. Read both the .rs and companion .md. Construct test cases: (1) definition with zero references, (2) reference with no definition, (3) definition referenced exactly once, (4) definition referenced in a comment but not structurally, (5) circular reference between two definitions. Run each through the rule and verify the expected pass/fail. Compare detected orphans against a manually computed ground truth.
**Pass criteria**: Rule reports all orphaned definitions and all undefined references; no false negatives on the 5 test cases above; circular references are handled without infinite loops; output identifies orphan by name and location.
**Fail criteria**: Any orphan pattern produces a false negative; rule panics on circular references; output does not identify orphan location; rule silently skips entities with unusual naming.

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Malformed evidence locator — parse error vs silent ignore
description:
**Audit Area**: error-handling-robustness
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Failure mode**: An evidence locator string is syntactically invalid (e.g. missing scheme, malformed URI, unsupported locator type)
**Expected behavior**: Parser returns a typed error identifying which part of the locator is invalid; the error propagates to the user with the offending string highlighted; silent ignore is not acceptable
**Current risk**: A lenient parser may accept malformed locators and store them, causing failures only at resolution time with no pointer back to the original bad input; or a strict parser may panic on unexpected input shapes

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Lock/unlock state machine: pre-conditions enforced before state change
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: Locking a claim that has unresolved dependencies or is already locked should be rejected before any state mutation occurs. If pre-conditions are checked after partial mutation, the store can enter an inconsistent state.
**What to check**: In src/model.rs, find the lock and unlock transition handlers. Verify that all pre-condition checks (entity exists, current state allows lock, no conflicting pending operations) are performed before any event is appended to the store. Check that the lock operation is atomic: either all pre-conditions pass and the event is written, or no event is written. Verify unlock has symmetric pre-conditions. Check integration tests for: locking an already-locked entity, unlocking a non-locked entity, locking a non-existent entity.
**Pass criteria**: All pre-conditions checked before store mutation; lock/unlock operations are atomic (all-or-nothing); each invalid pre-condition produces a distinct, descriptive error; 3 invalid-precondition tests exist.
**Fail criteria**: Any state mutation occurs before all pre-conditions are verified; lock on already-locked entity silently succeeds; error messages are generic (e.g., 'operation failed') without identifying the violated pre-condition.
close_reason: Audit complete: lock/unlock pre-conditions are sound. 2 integration tests added. No production bugs found.

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Circular dependency in trace — does not hang or stack overflow
description:
**Audit Area**: error-handling-robustness
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Failure mode**: The claim or rule graph contains a cycle (claim A supports claim B which supports claim A), and the trace or explain command traverses it
**Expected behavior**: Cycle detection (e.g. visited set) terminates traversal immediately and reports the cycle members; no infinite loop, no stack overflow from unbounded recursion
**Current risk**: Recursive graph traversal without a visited guard will exhaust the stack on cycles; the program will crash with a stack overflow rather than a user-facing error

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Empty project — commands that require data handle empty state
description:
**Audit Area**: error-handling-robustness
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Failure mode**: A freshly initialized project has no claims, rules, or evidence; commands like list, trace, stats, or export are run immediately after init
**Expected behavior**: Each command emits a friendly empty-state message (e.g. 'No claims yet. Run `dont add` to get started.') rather than an error or blank output; no panics from unwrap() on empty collections
**Current risk**: Iterator::first().unwrap() or indexing into empty Vecs may panic; empty table formatters may produce malformed output

title: [DOCS-QUALITY] Audit EVALUATION_REPORT_DOCS.md criteria against current docs
description:
**Audit Area**: documentation-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Doc file**: docs/EVALUATION_REPORT_DOCS.md
**What to verify**: For each evaluation criterion listed in EVALUATION_REPORT_DOCS.md, assess whether the current documentation actually satisfies it; identify criteria marked as passing that are no longer met, and criteria marked as failing that have since been addressed; produce an updated pass/fail assessment
**Quality criteria**: EVALUATION_REPORT_DOCS.md reflects the current state of the documentation suite; no criterion is incorrectly marked; the report can be used as a live quality gate rather than a historical snapshot
close_reason: Both L5-01 (missing tutorial) and L5-02 (modality contamination) are resolved. tutorial.md exists and covers the full workflow; grounding-workflow.md is cleanly procedural with rationale moved to purpose.md. Report updated: DEGRADED → HEALTHY, 0 open findings.

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Mode enforcement boundary: strict vs permissive mode gates operations
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: If strict mode does not actually gate the operations it should restrict, the mode system is theater. Users who configure strict mode for a project expect real enforcement, not a flag that is checked but never acted upon.
**What to check**: Read src/project.rs for mode representation and src/main.rs or rule dispatch for mode-gated operations. For each operation claimed to be restricted in strict mode, verify the check is performed before the operation executes (not after). Verify the check reads the persisted mode rather than a default. Test: run a restricted operation in permissive mode (should succeed), then switch to strict mode and re-run (should fail with a clear mode-related error). Verify the error names the mode and the operation.
**Pass criteria**: Every mode-gated operation checks the current project mode before executing; strict mode rejects restricted operations with a message naming the mode; switching mode is reflected immediately in subsequent operations.
**Fail criteria**: Any mode-gated operation executes without checking the mode; mode check reads a hardcoded default instead of persisted state; error message on rejection does not mention mode.

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Term label validation completeness: SK11 format edge cases covered
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: Term labels following the SK11 format are used as identifiers throughout the system. If the validator accepts malformed labels, downstream lookups silently fail or produce spurious matches.
**What to check**: Read the term label validator in src/config.rs. Identify the full SK11 format specification (prefix, separator, numeric suffix, length limits). Test the validator against: all-lowercase label, all-uppercase label, missing prefix, missing numeric suffix, suffix with leading zeros, suffix exceeding max digits, separator variants (dash vs underscore vs dot), labels with spaces, and empty string. Verify each invalid case returns a descriptive Err.
**Pass criteria**: Validator rejects every malformed SK11 variant with an error naming the violated rule; valid SK11 labels pass; edge cases (leading zeros, max-length, unicode) are explicitly tested.
**Fail criteria**: Any malformed SK11 label passes validation; valid labels are rejected; no unit tests for edge cases; error message does not identify which SK11 rule was violated.
close_reason: 24 unit tests added for SK11 label validator helpers. All edge cases pass — validator already sound.

title: [DOCS-QUALITY] Verify hypotheses.md lifecycle matches implementation
description:
**Audit Area**: documentation-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Doc file**: docs/hypotheses.md
**What to verify**: Trace the documented hypothesis lifecycle states (e.g. proposed, active, grounded, rejected) through the actual source code; confirm that every state transition described in the doc is reachable via CLI commands; check that status labels, command names, and output formats shown in examples match current behavior
**Quality criteria**: Lifecycle diagram or description in hypotheses.md maps 1:1 to states representable in the data model and reachable via the CLI; no phantom states or missing transitions documented

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Permission errors — read-only filesystem handled gracefully
description:
**Audit Area**: error-handling-robustness
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Failure mode**: The .dont/ directory or store file is owned by another user, or the filesystem is mounted read-only (e.g. in a container or CI environment)
**Expected behavior**: IO errors from permission-denied are caught and reported with the file path and a clear message distinguishing 'file not found' from 'permission denied'; read-only commands (list, explain, completions) continue to work
**Current risk**: Rust std::io::Error surfaces as an opaque 'Os error 13' with no human-readable context; write commands may silently fail or corrupt a partial write

title: [DOCS-QUALITY] Verify enforcement.md accurately documents enforcement mode behavior
description:
**Audit Area**: documentation-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Doc file**: docs/enforcement.md
**What to verify**: Compare each documented enforcement mode (e.g. warn, error, off) against the actual behavior produced by the CLI; verify that documented exit codes, output formats, and config options match the implementation in src/; check that any config file examples in the doc are valid and produce the described effect
**Quality criteria**: Every enforcement mode documented produces exactly the described behavior; config snippets are valid and tested; exit code table matches actual binary exit codes
close_reason: enforcement.md had two inaccuracies: prime was described as exiting 0 silently when clean (it always prints status) and the lockability rule was called always-strict (the rule engine severity is Warn; enforcement is via in-code gate)

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Evidence locator parsing robustness: malformed locators must not panic
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: Evidence locators are user-supplied strings. Any panic in the parser on malformed input is a user-facing crash. The parser must handle all malformed inputs gracefully and return structured errors.
**What to check**: Find the evidence locator parser (likely in src/model.rs, src/config.rs, or a dedicated module). Run the parser against: empty string, string with no separator, string with multiple separators, unicode characters, extremely long strings (>1000 chars), strings with null bytes, and strings with only whitespace. Verify none of these inputs call panic!(), unwrap(), or index out of bounds. Check whether there is a fuzz target or property test for the parser.
**Pass criteria**: Parser returns Err for all malformed inputs without panicking; error message identifies the malformed portion; at least one test per invalid category listed above exists.
**Fail criteria**: Any malformed input causes a panic, index out of bounds, or stack overflow; parser silently succeeds on inputs that should be rejected; no test for empty or whitespace-only locator.
close_reason: Audit verified: parse_line_span is robust. 26 unit tests added covering all malformed input categories. No bugs found.

title: [DOCS-QUALITY] Verify rule documentation cross-references are correct
description:
**Audit Area**: documentation-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Doc file**: src/rules/*.md
**What to verify**: Identify every 'See also', 'Related rules', or inline cross-reference in rule .md files; confirm each referenced rule name matches an existing rule identifier; check that bidirectional references are consistent (if rule A references rule B, verify rule B also references A where appropriate)
**Quality criteria**: No broken rule references; all rule IDs used in cross-references exist in the codebase; related-rule links are symmetric where the relationship is mutual

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Import adapter network errors — graceful failure with retry hints
description:
**Audit Area**: robustness — import adapter network errors and timeout behavior

**What to test**: Two distinct failure modes must both be handled gracefully:
- (a) Connection refused / DNS failure → immediate error surfaced to the user with the failing URL and error kind
- (b) Slow server / unresponsive host → bounded wait with a timeout error, not an indefinite hang

**Pass criteria**:
- `dont import` fails within 30 seconds maximum even when the target host is completely unresponsive
- Each error surfaces the URL that failed, the error kind (timeout vs. DNS vs. connection refused vs. TLS), and a suggested action (retry, check connectivity, use --offline flag)
- No panic, no silent partial import with no indication of skipped records

**Test approach**:
- For (a): point the import adapter at a non-existent hostname or a locally refused port; verify an immediate, descriptive error
- For (b): mock a slow server (e.g. `nc -l` that accepts the connection but never responds) or use a non-routable IP (e.g. 192.0.2.1 — TEST-NET); verify the process exits with a timeout error within 30 seconds

title: [CLI-CONSISTENCY] Command abbreviations and aliases — consistent where provided
description:
**Audit Area**: cli-consistency
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to verify**: Any command aliases or abbreviations are documented, behave identically to their canonical forms, and appear in completions and --help
**Affected commands**: all commands that have or could have aliases; specifically audit atom (define/dismiss sub-actions), hypothesis (add/assess sub-actions), rules (list/show/add/test sub-actions)
**Consistency rule**: Aliases must be listed in --help alongside the canonical name; aliases must produce identical output and exit codes; aliases must appear in shell completions; no undocumented aliases should exist; if a command has no alias, --help must not imply one exists
close_reason: Aligned alias help/completion coverage and corrected flag help to document term support; verified with cargo test

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Project initialization error paths: all failure modes handled
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: Project init is the first thing a user runs. If failure modes (directory already exists, permissions denied, config parse error, conflicting config) panic or produce cryptic messages, the user experience degrades immediately.
**What to check**: Read src/project.rs in full. Identify every I/O operation (directory creation, file write, config read). For each, verify it uses ? or explicit error handling rather than .unwrap() or .expect(). Check that error messages are user-readable and identify the path or operation that failed. Verify integration tests cover: init in an already-initialized directory, init with read-only filesystem (simulate via permissions or mocking), and init with a malformed pre-existing config.
**Pass criteria**: No .unwrap() or .expect() in project.rs; all error messages name the failed operation and path; at least 3 failure-mode integration tests pass.
**Fail criteria**: Any .unwrap()/.expect() in project init code paths; error messages expose Rust internals (e.g., Os { code: 13 }); missing tests for already-initialized or permission-denied scenarios.

title: [CLI-CONSISTENCY] --help output format consistent structure across all commands
description:
**Audit Area**: cli-consistency
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to verify**: Every command's --help output follows the same structural template: description, usage line, arguments section, flags section, examples section
**Affected commands**: init, conclude, define, ground, flag, trust, undoubt, ignore, reopen, forget, show, why, list, trace, prime, atom, hypothesis, rules, explain, import, completions, version
**Consistency rule**: Help sections appear in fixed order: (1) short description, (2) Usage: <command> [OPTIONS] <ARGS>, (3) Arguments section with descriptions, (4) Options/Flags section, (5) at least one Example; no command omits examples; description tense is consistent (imperative, e.g. 'Record a claim' not 'Records a claim'); line length does not exceed 80 chars
close_reason: Added Examples sections across CLI help surface and regression coverage for command help structure; verified with cargo test

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Very long evidence excerpts — no truncation bugs or panics
description:
**Audit Area**: error-handling-robustness
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Failure mode**: An evidence excerpt field contains tens of thousands of characters (e.g. a pasted paper abstract or log dump)
**Expected behavior**: Storage accepts the full content without size limit panic; display truncates gracefully at a configurable column width with an ellipsis; serialization round-trips without corruption
**Current risk**: Fixed-size buffers or display formatters may panic on index out of bounds; very large excerpts may bloat the store and slow all reads

title: [DOCS-QUALITY] Audit lib.rs public API for documentation coverage
description:
**Audit Area**: documentation-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Doc file**: src/lib.rs
**What to verify**: Run cargo doc --no-deps and inspect the generated output; flag every pub fn, pub struct, pub enum, and pub trait that is missing a doc comment; confirm module-level docs describe the library's intended programmatic use; check that doc-test examples compile and pass
**Quality criteria**: All public items have doc comments; cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items produces no 'missing documentation' warnings for public items; at least one doc-test example exists per major public type

title: [TEST-COVERAGE] stdin pipe with multiple items — batch processing
description:
**Audit Area**: test-coverage
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Gap**: tests/stdin_pipe.rs tests single-item stdin input but does not cover batch processing (multiple newline-delimited items piped in one invocation).
**Test strategy**: Add tests piping 5+ items via stdin: assert all items are processed and appear in store, partial failures (one malformed item among valid ones) produce per-item errors without aborting the batch, exit code reflects whether any item failed, and --json output lists per-item results in an array envelope.
**Risk if missing**: Batch stdin processing could silently truncate after the first item, fail atomically on any error (losing valid items), or produce non-parseable mixed output.
close_reason: 5+ item batch, partial failure, all-invalid tests added; all pass

title: [CLI-CONSISTENCY] Color/no-color output — consistent TTY detection across commands
description:
**Audit Area**: cli-consistency
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to verify**: ANSI color codes are emitted only when stdout is a TTY; color is suppressed when piping, redirecting, or when NO_COLOR env var is set; --color/--no-color flags override TTY detection consistently
**Affected commands**: show, why, list, trace, prime, atom, hypothesis, rules, explain (any command with formatted human-readable output)
**Consistency rule**: Color on TTY by default; no color when stdout is not a TTY; NO_COLOR=1 disables color globally; --no-color flag disables color for a single invocation; --color flag forces color even in pipes; no command hard-codes color escape codes without checking TTY/env
close_reason: Added global --color/--no-color overrides and tests for env/flag precedence; verified with cargo test

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Envelope output consistency: all commands produce envelope on --json
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: If any command silently omits the JSON envelope wrapper when --json is passed, consumers of the CLI's machine-readable output receive inconsistent schemas, breaking scripts and integrations.
**What to check**: Read src/envelope.rs to understand the envelope schema (version, status, data, errors fields). Then audit src/main.rs for every subcommand handler. Verify that when --json is present, every code path (including error paths) writes output through the envelope serializer rather than printing raw text. Check the 32 integration tests in tests/ for --json coverage across all subcommands.
**Pass criteria**: Every subcommand produces a valid, schema-consistent envelope when --json is passed, including on error; no subcommand writes raw stdout when --json is active; envelope schema version is present in every response.
**Fail criteria**: Any subcommand bypasses envelope on --json; error paths print plain text instead of envelope; envelope version field is missing or inconsistent across commands.

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Unicode in claim names — non-ASCII identifiers handled correctly
description:
**Audit Area**: error-handling-robustness
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Failure mode**: Claim names, tags, or evidence excerpts contain emoji, CJK characters, RTL text, zero-width joiners, or combining diacritics
**Expected behavior**: All string operations (display, truncation, slug generation, fuzzy search) are Unicode-aware and do not split multibyte sequences; output is correctly aligned in the terminal
**Current risk**: Byte-indexed slicing may panic on multibyte chars; display width assumptions break for wide characters; slug generation may produce invalid identifiers

title: [TEST-COVERAGE] dont lock — gate pre-conditions enforced
description:
**Audit Area**: test-coverage
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Gap**: tests/lock.rs covers the lock operation itself but does not verify that gate pre-conditions (e.g., required evidence present, minimum trust level met, no open hypotheses) are enforced before the lock is applied.
**Test strategy**: Add tests for each documented gate condition: attempt to lock when condition is unmet and assert rejection with descriptive reason, then satisfy the condition and assert lock succeeds. Also test that --json wraps gate-failure errors in the envelope.
**Risk if missing**: Lock gates that fail to enforce pre-conditions allow premature or invalid locking of claims, undermining the epistemic integrity guarantees of the tool.
close_reason: Covered by existing tests in lock.rs and show_list.rs respectively

title: [DOCS-QUALITY] Verify contributing guide presence and accuracy
description:
**Audit Area**: documentation-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Doc file**: CONTRIBUTING.md (or docs/contributing.md)
**What to verify**: Confirm a contributing guide exists; check that it covers: setting up the dev environment, running tests, code style requirements, PR process, and how to add a new rule; verify all commands in the guide still work
**Quality criteria**: Contributing guide exists, is findable from the README, and gives a complete path from clone to first passing PR without gaps or outdated commands

title: [CLI-CONSISTENCY] Positional argument conventions consistent across commands
description:
**Audit Area**: cli-consistency
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to verify**: Positional arguments follow consistent conventions for ordering, naming in help text, and behavior when omitted or given extras
**Affected commands**: define, ground, flag, trust, undoubt, ignore, reopen, forget, show, why, trace, atom, hypothesis, rules, explain, import
**Consistency rule**: First positional is always the primary identifier (claim-id, rule-name, etc.); subsequent positionals are secondary data; usage strings use angle brackets for required (<claim-id>) and square brackets for optional ([note]); extra positional args produce an actionable error, not silent discard; no command uses positional args where flags would be clearer
close_reason: Standardized positional argument value names across commands and added regression coverage for help usage and extra-arg errors.

title: [CLI-CONSISTENCY] Completions accuracy — output matches actual CLI surface
description:
**Audit Area**: cli-consistency
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to verify**: Shell completions generated for all supported shells (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, powershell) accurately reflect the current command surface — all subcommands, all flags, and all subcommand-specific flags
**Affected commands**: completions (and the entire CLI surface it must describe)
**Consistency rule**: Completions must include every top-level command and every subcommand of atom, hypothesis, and rules; flag completions must list the correct flags per command; completions must be regenerated and re-audited whenever a command or flag is added or removed; stale completions are a consistency failure

title: [DOCS-QUALITY] Verify mdBook build compiles without errors
description:
**Audit Area**: documentation-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Doc file**: book.toml, docs/SUMMARY.md
**What to verify**: Run mdbook build from the project root; confirm zero errors and zero unresolved links; verify SUMMARY.md lists every file in docs/ and that all referenced paths exist on disk; check that the rendered book has correct navigation ordering
**Quality criteria**: mdbook build exits 0 with no warnings; all pages render; no dead internal links; SUMMARY.md is complete and ordered logically
close_reason: mdbook build exits 0 with no warnings. All 9 SUMMARY.md pages render to HTML. All internal links resolve to existing files. No dead links, no missing files, no SUMMARY.md gaps found.

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Concurrent access — two processes writing to same store
description:
**Audit Area**: robustness — concurrent store access

**What to test**: Does `dont` enforce single-writer semantics, or does it use file locking? Two `dont` processes writing concurrently to the same store must not silently corrupt the event log.

**Pass criteria**: One of the following must be true:
- (a) File locking (advisory or mandatory) prevents interleaved writes — second writer waits or fails with a clear 'store is locked' message
- (b) Last-write-wins is the documented and deliberate behavior, with a warning in the docs about concurrent use
- (c) An advisory warning is emitted at startup when the store is already open

Data corruption with no error message is a hard failure regardless of which strategy is chosen.

**Test approach**: Launch two `dont assert` processes concurrently targeting the same store. After both exit, read back the store and verify: all events are present and parseable, no interleaved/partial records exist, and no silent data loss occurred.

title: [CLI-CONSISTENCY] version output format matches JSON envelope spec
description:
**Audit Area**: cli-consistency
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to verify**: The version command's plain and --json output formats match the documented envelope spec; version string follows semver; --json envelope includes version, name, and any build metadata fields
**Affected commands**: version
**Consistency rule**: Plain output: single line 'dont <semver>'; --json output: valid JSON matching the envelope schema with at minimum {"version": "<semver>", "name": "dont"}; no extra prose mixed into --json output; exit code 0 always
close_reason: Version JSON payload updated to {version, name: 'dont'} per spec; tests added in tests/invocation_flags.rs (commit 622b1b9)

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Rule engine trait contract: all rules implement full trait
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: If the rule trait has required methods but some rule implementations provide stub or default no-op implementations, the rule engine silently skips checks, producing false negatives. Every rule must implement the complete contract.
**What to check**: Identify the rule trait definition (likely in src/rules/ or src/lib.rs). List all required methods. For each of the 8 rule implementations in src/rules/, verify every required method has a non-stub implementation (not just todo!(), unimplemented!(), or an empty block returning Ok(())). Check that the .md companion file for each rule matches the implemented behavior. Also verify rules are registered in any central rule registry or dispatch table.
**Pass criteria**: All 8 rules implement every required trait method with real logic; no todo!() or unimplemented!() in any rule; each rule's .md matches its .rs behavior.
**Fail criteria**: Any rule has a stub method body; any required trait method returns a constant Ok(()) without inspection; a rule exists in src/rules/ but is not registered in the engine.

title: [TEST-COVERAGE] dont show — missing entity error handling
description:
**Audit Area**: test-coverage
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Gap**: tests/entity_lookup.rs covers successful entity resolution but does not assert the exact error behavior when `dont show <id>` is called with a nonexistent entity ID.
**Test strategy**: Add tests for: nonexistent ID returns non-zero exit, error message names the missing ID, --json wraps the error in envelope (not raw text), and a partially-matching ID (prefix ambiguity) produces an informative disambiguation error.
**Risk if missing**: Missing-entity errors could print nothing, panic, or return exit code 0, misleading scripts and users into thinking the show succeeded.
close_reason: Already covered by entity_lookup/empty_state/show_list tests; verified with cargo test

title: [TEST-COVERAGE] dont list — all filter combinations
description:
**Audit Area**: test-coverage
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Gap**: tests/show_list.rs covers basic listing but does not systematically test filter flag combinations (e.g., --status + --tag, --author + --since, --type + --status).
**Test strategy**: Add parameterized or table-driven tests for: each filter flag in isolation, at least three two-flag combinations, and a three-flag combination. Assert result set is correctly narrowed, zero-result case returns empty list (not error), and --json wraps filtered results correctly.
**Risk if missing**: Filter interaction bugs (AND vs OR logic, flag precedence) would only be caught by manual QA, allowing incorrect result sets to ship.
close_reason: Covered by existing tests in lock.rs and show_list.rs respectively

title: [DOCS-QUALITY] Audit error messages for actionability and clarity
description:
**Audit Area**: documentation-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Doc file**: src/main.rs, src/rules/
**What to verify**: Enumerate all user-facing error messages in the codebase; for each, assess whether it names the problem, explains the cause, and tells the user what to do next; flag messages that are cryptic, reference internal identifiers, or provide no recovery path
**Quality criteria**: Every error message answers: what went wrong, why, and how to fix it; no raw Rust type names or internal paths leak into user-visible errors

title: [ROBUSTNESS] Invalid claim references — referencing non-existent entities
description:
**Audit Area**: error-handling-robustness
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Failure mode**: A command references a claim ID, rule name, or evidence key that does not exist in the store
**Expected behavior**: Clear 'not found' error that names the missing entity and its type; optionally suggests similar names via fuzzy match
**Current risk**: Rules engine or trace logic may propagate a None/unwrap leading to a panic, or silently skip the missing entity and produce an incomplete result

title: [CLI-CONSISTENCY] Input validation error messages — consistent format and actionability
description:
**Audit Area**: cli-consistency
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**What to verify**: All input validation errors follow a consistent format: what was wrong, what was expected, and (where possible) a suggested fix or example
**Affected commands**: define, ground, flag, trust, undoubt, ignore, reopen, forget, show, why, trace, atom, hypothesis, rules, explain, import, completions
**Consistency rule**: Error messages must include: (1) the field/argument that failed validation, (2) the reason it failed, (3) the expected format or valid values; errors go to stderr; format should be 'error: <field>: <reason>; expected <format>'; no raw Rust panics or unwrap traces exposed to users

title: [SPEC-ALIGN] dont-lifecycle-verbs: available state transition verbs match spec
description:
**Audit Area**: spec-alignment
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Spec**: dont-lifecycle-verbs
**What to verify**: Every verb (assert, retract, ground, challenge, resolve, etc.) defined in dont-lifecycle-verbs is available as a CLI command with the specified semantics, preconditions, and postconditions
**Mismatch risk**: Verbs missing from CLI, verb aliases differ, precondition enforcement absent, postcondition side-effects not applied as specified

title: [TEST-COVERAGE] JSON envelope on error cases
description:
**Audit Area**: test-coverage
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Gap**: tests/envelope.rs validates the happy-path JSON envelope schema but does not assert that error responses (non-zero exits, validation failures, not-found cases) are also wrapped in the correct envelope structure when --json is passed.
**Test strategy**: For each major command, add --json + error-triggering input test: confirm the response is valid JSON, contains a status field indicating failure, and includes an error message field. Cover at minimum: not-found entity, invalid argument, and store-read-failure scenarios.

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Model state machine completeness: invalid transitions rejected
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5
**Why this matters**: If the state machine in src/model.rs does not exhaustively reject invalid transitions, entities can reach logically impossible states (e.g., re-flagging an already-locked claim). These silent no-ops or panics are hard to debug in production.
**What to check**: Map all states and all transition operations (flag, ignore, lock, reopen, trust, undoubt) into a transition matrix. For each (state, operation) pair that is invalid, verify the code returns an Err rather than silently succeeding or panicking. Check that the error message identifies the current state and the attempted transition. Verify integration tests in tests/ cover at least the key invalid paths: flagging a locked entity, reopening a trusted entity, etc.
**Pass criteria**: Every invalid (state, transition) pair returns a typed Err with a message; no .unwrap() on state checks; test coverage for at least 6 invalid transition paths.
**Fail criteria**: Any invalid transition silently succeeds, panics, or returns Ok(()); error messages do not describe the invalid transition.

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Config validation completeness: all fields validated on parse
description:

**What to check**: Read src/config.rs in full. For each struct field, trace whether validation (range checks, format checks, non-empty checks) happens inside the FromStr/Deserialize impl or is deferred to call sites. **Pass criteria**: Every config field is validated at parse/deserialization time; invalid values produce errors naming the field and constraint; no field silently accepts an invalid value and panics later.

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Store invariant enforcement: event log ordering guarantee
description:
**Audit Area**: code-quality
**Epic**: dont-4k5

**What to check**: Read src/store.rs in full. Verify that (1) each append operation uses a monotonic sequence or timestamp, (2) concurrent writes are prevented or serialized, (3) there are no code paths that insert events out of order, (4) the replay function iterates events in insertion order. Also check whether integration tests in tests/ exercise concurrent or interleaved append scenarios.
**Pass criteria**: Store appends are atomic and ordered; replay always produces deterministic state; tests cover at least one out-of-order or concurrent scenario.
**Fail criteria**: No ordering guarantee at the persistence layer; replay order depends on filesystem or HashMap iteration; no test covers ordering edge cases.

title: [CODE-QUALITY] Error type hierarchy: anyhow overuse vs typed errors in public API
description:

title: Add ephemeral session wrapper for transient investigation work
description:
## Why

Debug and investigation sessions produce evidence that is useful in the moment but should not persist to .dont/ or trigger git commits. An ephemeral session wrapper provides isolated transient storage that is discarded on session end.

## What

'dont session start --ephemeral' / 'dont session end' commands create an isolated session with relaxed --file rules. Propagation via env var. No writes to .dont/; no git operations.

## Session Lifecycle

1. 'dont session start --ephemeral'
   - Creates session dir at '$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dont/sessions/<session-id>/'
   - Prints: 'export DONT_EPHEMERAL_SESSION_ID=<session-id>' (user must eval or run manually)
   - All subsequent 'dont'/'dt' commands check DONT_EPHEMERAL_SESSION_ID

2. Inside session:
   - All reads/writes go to session dir (not .dont/)
   - No git commits
   - --file: clean files → 'git:<sha>'; dirty files → 'content:<sha256>'; untracked → always reject
   - Provenance: 'session_id: "ephemeral:<session-id>"' (prefix disambiguates from spawn session_id)

3. 'dont session end'
   - Discards session dir
   - Prints: 'unset DONT_EPHEMERAL_SESSION_ID'

4. 'dont session end --export <path>'
   - Serializes all ephemeral claims to portable snapshot at <path>
   - Then discards session dir

## Storage Separation

- Ephemeral sessions: '$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/dont/sessions/<session-id>/' (OS-managed, lost on reboot)
- Spawn requests (existing): '.dont/sessions/' — NOT affected; different path, different purpose

## Propagation

Env var 'DONT_EPHEMERAL_SESSION_ID':
- Set by: 'dont session start --ephemeral' (printed for user to eval)
- Checked by: all dont/dt commands before determining storage target
- Cleared by: 'dont session end' (printed for user to run 'unset')

## --file Behavior Summary

| Context | File state | Result |
|---------|-----------|--------|
| Persistent | clean | git:<sha> ✓ |
| Persistent | dirty/staged/untracked | reject |
| Ephemeral | clean | git:<sha> ✓ |
| Ephemeral | dirty | content:<sha256> ✓ |
| Ephemeral | staged | content:<sha256> ✓ |
| Ephemeral | untracked | reject |

## Acceptance

- 'dont session start --ephemeral' prints eval-able env var
- 'dont flag <id> --file dirty.md' inside session → locator has content:<sha256>
- 'dont flag <id> --file clean.md' inside session → locator has git:<sha>
- 'dont flag <id> --file untracked.md' inside session → rejected
- 'dont session end' discards session; subsequent commands use .dont/
- 'dont session end --export /tmp/findings.json' saves snapshot then discards
- Spawn 'session_id' in .dont/sessions/ unaffected
notes: CLRT-003: --export format = JSON, same claim schema as .dont/claims/*.json, with ephemeral:true flag on each claim. EXEC-001 (HITL): user must eval the printed env var — document as 'eval $(dont session start --ephemeral)'. ALIGN-001: Spec ref → dont-cli-core/spec.md (session commands).

title: Add 'dt' binary alias with strictly-separated positive-framing vocabulary
description:
## Why

'dont' reads as "do not" — epistemically humble framing. Some users want a positive-framing interface that is easier to reason about. 'dt' provides this as a strict-separate alias: wrong vocabulary fails with a helpful suggestion.

## What

Single binary detects 'argv[0]'. When invoked as 'dt', applies positive-framing command names. Wrong-vocabulary calls are errors (not silent aliases).

## Vocabulary Mapping

### Exclusive to 'dont' (error if called via 'dt'):
- 'dont conclude'  — error: "unknown command 'conclude' for dt. Did you mean 'dt record'?"
- 'dont trust'     — error: "unknown command 'trust' for dt. Did you mean 'dt challenge'?"
- 'dont forget'    — error: "unknown command 'forget' for dt. Did you mean 'dt lock'?"

### Exclusive to 'dt' (error if called via 'dont'):
- 'dt record'    — error: "unknown command 'record' for dont. Did you mean 'dont conclude'?"
- 'dt challenge' — error: "unknown command 'challenge' for dont. Did you mean 'dont trust'?"
- 'dt lock'      — error: "unknown command 'lock' for dont. Did you mean 'dont forget'?"

### Shared (valid in both, same behavior):
define, flag, dismiss, ground, ignore, undoubt, reopen, show, why, list, vocab,
prime, doctor, schema, examples, suggest-term, import, completions, help,
assume, overlook, guess, verify-evidence

## Implementation

- Single binary; 'argv[0]' determines active interface
- 'dont install' creates both 'dont' and 'dt' symlinks/binaries
- Error format: "unknown command '<cmd>' for <dont|dt>. Did you mean '<other-alias> <equivalent>'?"
- Help output labels itself with the invocation name

## Acceptance

- 'dt record "claim text"' succeeds (equivalent to 'dont conclude')
- 'dt challenge <id>' succeeds (equivalent to 'dont trust')
- 'dt lock <id>' succeeds (equivalent to 'dont forget')
- 'dt conclude ...' → error with 'dt record' suggestion
- 'dont record ...' → error with 'dont conclude' suggestion
- 'dt show <id>' works (shared command)
- 'dont show <id>' works (shared command)
- Installing 'dont' also installs 'dt' in the same bin directory
notes: CLRT-002: Verified shared vocabulary list against dont-cli-surface/spec.md at edb2c23. Shared commands (define, flag, dismiss, ground, ignore, undoubt, reopen, show, why, list, vocab, prime, doctor, import, completions, help, verify-evidence, trace, stats, export, atom, hypothesis, rules, explain) not listed as exclusive → remain valid in both interfaces. dt-exclusive: record, challenge, lock. dont-exclusive: conclude, trust, forget.
close_reason: Implemented dt binary alias with argv[0] detection. dt record/challenge/lock route to dont conclude/trust/forget. Cross-vocab errors give suggestions. All 10 acceptance tests pass.

title: --file evidence must capture git provenance; reject uncommitted/dirty files
description:
## Why

Without git provenance, file evidence is not reproducible — a fingerprint alone cannot prove what commit the file came from. Requiring a git SHA pins evidence to a verifiable repo state.

## What

Add a 'commit_ref' field to the repo-file locator schema. Use a prefixed format to distinguish provenance source:
- 'git:<sha>' — file is committed and clean (no unstaged diffs)
- 'content:<sha256>' — file content hash, used when file is dirty (ephemeral sessions only)

## Schema Extension

Add to repo-file locator:
  commit_ref?: string  // "git:<sha>" | "content:<sha256>"

This is additive. 'fingerprint' remains for drift detection (different purpose).

## Rejection Rules (persistent context)

Always reject --file if any of:
1. File is untracked (no git history)
2. File is staged but not yet committed (no SHA exists)
3. File has unstaged diffs (SHA would not match current content)

## Ephemeral Context (see ephemeral session issue)

Inside an ephemeral session:
- Clean file → 'git:<sha>' (preferred, same as persistent)
- Dirty file → 'content:<sha256>' (fallback, not an error)
- Untracked → always reject (even ephemeral)

## Acceptance

- 'dont flag <id> --file path/to/clean.md' → locator includes 'commit_ref: "git:<sha>"'
- 'dont flag <id> --file path/to/dirty.md' (persistent) → refused with clear error
- 'dont flag <id> --file path/to/staged.md' → refused
- 'dont flag <id> --file path/to/untracked.md' → refused
notes: CLRT-004: Add 'Staged → content:<sha256> ✓' to ephemeral section (consistent with dont-w36 --file table). EXEC-002: Verify 'dont flag' is the actual subcommand for adding evidence against dont-cli-surface/spec.md before implementing. ALIGN-001: Spec ref → evidence-locators/spec.md (repo-file locator schema).

title: Rename 'dont lock' command to 'dont forget'
description:
## Why

'dont forget' reads as "do not forget" — permanently preserve this claim — which aligns with the tool's epistemically-humble naming convention. 'dont lock' has no equivalent English reading in the dont-framing.

## What

Rename the 'lock' command to 'forget' on the dont-side only. The persisted status value 'locked' and event kind 'locked' remain unchanged (renaming those is a separate breaking-change scope).

## Scope

- Command name: 'dont lock' → 'dont forget'
- Persisted state: unchanged ('locked')
- Event kind: unchanged ('locked')
- dt-side equivalent: 'dt lock' (per dt alias design — these are strict-separate)
- 'dont lock' errors: "unknown command 'lock'. Did you mean 'dont forget'?"
- 'dt forget' errors: "unknown command 'forget'. Did you mean 'dt lock'?"

## Preconditions (unchanged)

All four must hold for 'dont forget' to succeed:
1. Claim is in 'verified' state
2. At least 3 assessed hypotheses
3. At least 2 independent supporting evidence items
4. No integrity-compromising derived assessments (stale, compromised-support, dangling-dependency, unresolved-term)

## Acceptance

- 'dont forget <id>' succeeds when all preconditions met
- 'dont forget <id>' refused with same error messages as current 'dont lock'
- 'dont lock' produces unknown-command error with 'dont forget' suggestion
- 'dt lock <id>' also works (same preconditions)
- All help text, man pages, and error messages updated
