title: Wire CI gate and add claim discipline rationale to AGENTS.md
description:
## Why this issue exists

Once prime exits non-zero on doubted claims and real claims exist, the gate needs to be wired into CI and agents need to understand why they must use dont when making design assertions.

## What needs to be done

1. Add check-claims recipe to justfile:
   check-claims:
       dont prime
   (Once Step 0 is done, prime itself exits 1 on doubted claims — no jq filter needed)

2. Add check-claims as a dependency of the existing ci recipe

3. Add to AGENTS.md before the gate instruction:
   dont exists to prevent ungrounded assertions. When building dont, agents must use dont to track design claims before asserting them — not after. A claim made without grounding is the exact failure mode the tool is designed to catch. Create claims with dont conclude, define any CURIEs, then add evidence before proceeding. Claims in doubted status block CI.

4. Document mode x gate interaction: in permissive mode, unverified claims are allowed; only doubted claims block CI. In strict mode, the tool itself blocks — the gate is complementary for pre-push checks.

## Acceptance criteria
- ci recipe fails when any claim is doubted
- ci recipe passes when all claims are unverified or verified
- AGENTS.md explains why claim discipline is required (not just that it is)
notes:
Add to AGENTS.md:

Success metric (30-day retrospective): run 'dont list --status=verified' and count how many architectural claims are verified. If fewer than 60% are verified after 30 days, the discipline is not working and should be simplified or dropped. A claim with no evidence activity for 30+ days is a retirement candidate.

Claim retirement workflow: when a design decision is reversed or superseded, run 'dont doubt <id> --reason="<explanation>"' then close it. Do not leave stale verified claims accumulating — they erode trust in prime output.

The ci recipe should run: (1) 'dont prime' (exits 1 on doubted claims), (2) 'cargo test'. Both must pass. If no ci recipe exists, create one that chains these.
close_reason: check-claims recipe added to justfile and ci. AGENTS.md updated with rationale, mode×gate interaction, claim retirement workflow, and success metric. Committed in e2b4c13.

title: Create design intent claims for the 7 shipped rules paired with wai entries
description:
## Why this issue exists

Tests verify rule behavior but do not encode non-obvious design constraints — intent that, if reversed, would look like a reasonable cleanup to a future developer. Claims capture these constraints and surface via prime if violated.

## What needs to be done

For each of the 7 rules (ungrounded, unresolved-terms, stale-cascade, lockable, correlated-error, dangling-definition, term-nonfunctional-label), create one claim encoding a non-obvious design constraint not captured by tests.

Example for ungrounded rule: The ungrounded rule severity is mode-dependent by design — warn in permissive, strict in strict — because enforcing grounding at conclude time would break incremental onboarding. Ground this with spec §8.1 wai entry.

Only create claims where:
- The constraint is non-obvious (a reviewer might reverse it thinking it's a bug)
- A wai entry exists or is created in the same ticket to serve as evidence
- The test suite does NOT fully capture the intent

Do not create claims where the tests already express the full design intent.

## Acceptance criteria
- At least one design intent claim per rule (7 minimum)
- Each claim has a wai section reference as evidence
- Claims are in unverified or verified status (not doubted)
notes:
HITL: draft candidate constraints per rule first, then get human approval on which qualify as non-obvious before creating claims.

Constraint starters per rule (refine and ground before creating):
- unresolved-terms: CURIE resolution is deferred in permissive mode — a claim with an unknown CURIE is warned, not blocked at conclude time.
- stale-cascade: fires on evidence-reference change, not claim text change — a claim whose text is edited but evidence reference is unchanged does not trigger stale-cascade.
- lockable: lock is a claim-state gate (prevents conclude/dismiss on locked claims), not a data lock — concurrent writers are not protected.
- correlated-error: severity is additive across related rules — a claim triggering both ungrounded and correlated-error gets the higher combined severity.
- dangling-definition: fires only on terms used in active claims, not all defined terms — orphaned term definitions with no claim references are not flagged.
- term-nonfunctional-label: label mismatch is warn-only in permissive mode and strict in strict mode — not a blocking error by default.
close_reason: All 7 design-intent claims created and verified against rule source files

title: Replace dummy claims with real load-bearing architectural claims
description:
## Why this issue exists

The repo contains placeholder claims (The Earth is flat, etc.) that produce noise. Replacing them with real design decisions turns the claim database into a living epistemic log and exercises the full grounding ceremony.

## What needs to be done

1. Delete all dummy claims (dont doubt + dont close or direct db cleanup)
2. Create these 4 load-bearing claims, each with at least one evidence entry at creation time:
   - Permissive mode is the correct default because it lets projects onboard incrementally without blocking conclude on unresolved terms (ground: .wai/projects/dont/research/2026-04-20-dont-specification-v0-2-draft-status.md §8.1)

   - CozoDB with Datalog is the right rule engine for dont rule evaluation (ground: .wai datalog research entries)

Each claim must have at least one evidence entry at creation time so the ungrounded rule does not fire immediately.

## Acceptance criteria
- dont prime shows 0 doubted claims after this work
- All 4 claims are in verified or unverified (not doubted) status
- No dummy claims remain

The command dont help --tutorial does not exist — running it produces 'unrecognized subcommand --tutorial'. The hint is emitted unconditionally, so every agent session sees a broken suggestion.

Done when: dont prime output no longer contains a hint pointing to dont help --tutorial; if a tutorial hint is re-added it must point to a command that exists (e.g. once dont-zoc and dont-e7b land).

title: UX: conclude --depends-on accepts both term:ID and CURIE inconsistently
description:
dont conclude '...' --depends-on term:ID and dont conclude '...' --depends-on WB:P001 both succeed but produce different outcomes. The term:ID form warns 'unresolved-term-ref: term reference term:ID is not yet defined' even when the term exists in the store. The CURIE form (WB:P001) stores the CURIE string as a raw dependency reference string without resolving it to an entity. The API accepts two formats but handles them differently and inconsistently.

Spec ref: dont-data-model §"Entity structure" — only claim: and term: prefixed ULIDs are externally-addressable EntityId values. Raw CURIEs are not EntityIds. The depends-on argument should accept one canonical form (term:ID) and optionally resolve a CURIE to its term:ID before storing.

Done when:
- dont conclude --depends-on WB:P001 resolves WB:P001 to its term:ID before storing (or errors if the CURIE is ambiguous/not found)
- dont conclude --depends-on term:ID with an existing term does NOT warn 'not yet defined'
- The warn-unresolved-term-ref rule fires only when the CURIE genuinely has no matching term entity
- cargo test validation::depends_on_curie_resolution passes

title: UX: empty claim statement is accepted
description:
dont conclude "" creates a claim with an empty statement and exits 0. An empty statement is semantically meaningless — the tool's purpose is to force grounded claims, and an empty string cannot be grounded.

Spec ref: dont-lifecycle-verbs — conclude introduces an 'unverified claim'; an empty string is not a claim. dont-errors §validation error codes — this should produce a structured validation error.

Done when:
- dont conclude "" exits 1 with code 'empty-statement' or equivalent validation error
- The error envelope includes a remediation suggesting a non-empty statement
- cargo test validation::conclude_empty_statement passes

title: UX: list command has no status filter
description:
dont list returns all claims regardless of status. There is no --status or --kind filter flag. In a project with many claims, users cannot quickly see only unverified or doubted items. The dont prime blocking[] field shows some filtering logic exists; list should expose the same.

Spec ref: dont-cli-surface §"Stdin piping for bulk entity operations" implies batch query support; filtering is a natural companion. dont-derived-queries §PrimeView shows status-based grouping is already computed server-side.

Done when:
- dont list --status=unverified returns only unverified claims
- dont list --status=doubted returns only doubted claims
- dont list --status=verified returns only verified claims
- dont list --status=ignored returns only ignored claims
- Invalid --status value produces a structured validation error
- cargo test cli::list_status_filter passes

title: UX: list command does not show terms
description:
dont list only returns claims. There is no command to list defined terms. Users who run dont list after dont define will not see their terms and may assume define failed. The list output's envelope_kind is 'claims' which confirms this is claim-only by current implementation.

Spec ref: dont-cli-surface §"Stdin piping for bulk entity operations" treats both claims and terms as entities accessible by ID. dont-data-model §"Entity structure" — both claim: and term: are externally-addressable EntityId values and should be listable.

Done when:
- dont list --kind=terms (or dont terms, or dont list --all) lists defined term entities
- Output includes term id, curie, label, status fields
- dont list --kind=claims retains current behavior
- dont list (no flag) lists both or defaults to claims with a hint about --kind=terms
- cargo test cli::list_terms passes

title: UX: all output is JSON — no human-readable mode
description:
Every dont command emits a JSON envelope regardless of whether --json is passed. The --json flag exists but appears to have no effect — JSON is always the output format.

This violates dont-cli-surface §"Universal flags": --plain suppresses formatting; §"json flag emits structured envelope": human logging moves to stderr when --json is set, implying human-readable is the default. The spec treats JSON as opt-in, not default.

Done when:
- dont list (no flags) emits human-readable plain text summary
- dont list --json emits the JSON envelope
- dont list --plain emits uncoloured human-readable text
- dont list --json --plain emits JSON (json wins per spec)
- cargo test cli::output_format passes
notes: This issue is part of the 'improve-cli-ergonomics' OpenSpec change proposal.
close_reason: Added --human flag; human-readable output for all commands; --json takes precedence when both flags are set; 8 tests in tests/output_format.rs

comments.author: charly vibes
comments.text: QA confirmed: every command (init, conclude, list, show, etc.) currently emits JSON on stdout. Passing --json has no effect on the output format. Human-readable output is entirely missing.

title: UX: --reason shown as optional in help but enforced as required at runtime
description:
Both dont trust --help and dont ignore --help list -r, --reason without any indication it is required. At runtime, omitting --reason from either command produces a hard error (exit 1, code 'reason-required'). The help text should mark these flags as required so users are not surprised.

Spec ref: dont-cli-surface §"No short-flag conflicts" — help and completions must document short flags; dont-lifecycle-verbs §"Ignore requires a reason" and §"trust transition records its reason" both make reason non-optional.

Done when:
- dont trust --help output indicates --reason is required (e.g. via clap's required annotation rendering, or a note in the flag description)
- dont ignore --help output likewise indicates --reason is required
- cargo test cli::help_flags_reflect_required passes

title: Bug: internal error remediation references non-existent dont doctor
description:
When trust or dismiss is called on a term entity, the error envelope's remediation field points to dont doctor: {"command": "dont doctor", "description": "Run dont doctor to diagnose the issue"}. dont doctor does not exist as a subcommand. The remediation advice is therefore useless and erodes trust in the error system.

This is separate from the prime tutorial hint (see dont-e6m). The dont doctor command is tracked for future implementation in dont-xou, but until it lands, error remediations must not reference it.

Done when: the internal-error error record no longer suggests dont doctor as a remediation; dont-xou (implement dont doctor) can re-add the reference once the command exists.

title: Bug: prime status_counts excludes ignored entities
description:
dont prime reports ignored: 0 in status_counts even when there is at least one ignored claim. dont list returns the ignored entity correctly, so the data is present. The prime query appears to filter out ignored entities when computing status counts.

Spec ref: dont-derived-queries — PrimeView includes status_counts reflecting current project state. dont-status-lifecycle §"Locked and ignored states" — ignored is a valid persisted status in the shared lattice and should appear in counts.

Note: dont-status-lifecycle §"ignored entities are excluded from derived assessment output" applies to derived_assessments[], not to status_counts. The prime status_counts should include all statuses including ignored.

Done when:
- dont prime status_counts.ignored equals the actual count of entities with persisted status ignored
- cargo test derived::prime_status_counts_includes_ignored passes
close_reason: status_counts now iterates both claims and terms across all 5 statuses; locked=0 assertion added to test

title: Ignore .dont and add local install recipe
description: Update dont init to ensure .dont/ is ignored by git in initialized repositories, and add a just install recipe for local CLI testing. Done when init tests cover .gitignore update and just --list shows install.

title: Implement dont examples command
description:
Implement 'dont examples' as specified in dont-derived-queries. Returns canonical worked examples as ExamplesList payload. Examples are stored as assertions in the CozoDB graph and retrieved by a Datalog query.

Done when: `cargo test examples::list` passes; 'dont examples' emits a non-empty ExamplesList payload when examples have been asserted.

title: Implement dont spawns inspection command
description:
Implement 'dont spawns' with --pending, --timed-out, and --all flags as specified in dont-spawn-protocol. Returns a SpawnsList payload filtered by lifecycle state. This is a read-only query over the spawn state machine; it shares no implementation with expiry sweep logic.

Done when: `cargo test spawns::list` passes; 'dont spawns --pending' lists only pending entities; 'dont spawns --timed-out' lists only expired spawns.

title: Author Diataxis tutorial and how-to guide content for dont help
description:
Write the canonical tutorial and how-to guide content surfaced by 'dont help --tutorial' and 'dont help --howto <topic>' as specified in dont-agent-help. Tutorial follows Diataxis learning-oriented structure; how-to guides are task-oriented. This is a HITL authoring task, not AFK code generation.

Done when: 'dont help --tutorial' renders a complete onboarding tutorial; 'dont help --howto <topic>' returns accurate task-oriented guides for at least three topics.

title: Implement dont schema and dont examples commands
description:
Implement 'dont schema <name>' as specified in dont-derived-queries. Returns JSON Schema documents as SchemaDoc payload for the named vocabulary entity. Schema is derived from the CozoDB assertion graph.

Done when: `cargo test schema::resolve` passes; 'dont schema <name>' emits a valid SchemaDoc JSON payload for a known term.

title: Implement dont vocab term listing
description:
Implement 'dont vocab' as specified in dont-derived-queries. Returns terms with same filter semantics as 'dont list': --status, --derived-assessment, --as-of. Returns term_list envelope.

Done when: `cargo test derived::vocab` passes; 'dont vocab' emits a term_list with all defined terms; 'dont vocab --status=verified' returns only verified terms; 'dont vocab --as-of=<date>' returns the state at that timestamp.

title: Implement dont doctor substrate health check
description:
Implement 'dont doctor' as specified in dont-derived-queries. Reports DoctorReport: CLI version, substrate health checks, rule compilation status, auxiliary tool availability. --strict exits 1 on warnings or failures.

Done when: `cargo test derived::doctor` passes; 'dont doctor' emits a DoctorReport JSON envelope; a corrupt .dont/store emits a substrate health failure; 'dont doctor --strict' exits 1 when any check is non-green; all checks pass on a clean init.

title: Implement dont import linkml adapter
description:
Implement 'dont import linkml' as specified in dont-linkml-import. Subprocess-backed adapter over LinkML CLI. Lossy-by-design (grounding not round-tripping). Flattened features: is_a → kind_of chain, mixins flattened, slot_usage expanded. Warning-tier: permissible_values, string patterns. Refusal-tier: SPARQL expressions, reified slots. No partial import on refusal. Raises config-missing error if LinkML CLI is absent.

Done when: `cargo test import::linkml` passes (fixture schema); a valid LinkML schema imports with is_a flattened to kind_of chain; a schema with SPARQL expressions emits a structured refusal and imports nothing; missing LinkML CLI emits a config-missing error with install guidance.

title: Implement dont prime session-start orientation
description:
Implement 'dont prime' as specified in dont-derived-queries. Returns PrimeView: project mode, rule activation, status counts, assessment counts, blocking items, pending spawns, harness mode, and invariants. Designed for agent session-start orientation.

Done when: `cargo test derived::prime` passes; 'dont prime' emits a valid PrimeView JSON envelope; the view reflects current project state (status counts match actual entities); harness mode field reflects detection result from dont-a84.
notes: Note: dont prime is partially implemented — harness_mode, status_counts, and blocking[] already return data (verified via QA session 2026-05-06). The fields gated on dont-sap are those related to harness-mode detection specifics and spawn-surface fields. Consider splitting: close the unblocked subset now, or annotate which prime fields are gated on dont-sap vs already working.

title: Implement dont import ttl adapter
description:
Implement 'dont import ttl' (Turtle/RDF) adapter as specified in dont-import-adapters. Normalise Turtle input to dont import relations via shared import infrastructure (dont-3ul). Source-specific normalisation: parse prefixes from @prefix declarations; resolve IRIs to CURIEs using prefix registry; map rdfs:label / skos:prefLabel to term label; map rdfs:comment / skos:definition to definition; skip blank-node subjects (warning-tier, not refusal — blank nodes are idiomatic in Turtle); reject unparseable triples (refusal-tier).

Done when: `cargo test import::ttl` passes; a Turtle file with prefixed IRIs imports cleanly; blank-node subjects produce warnings only.

title: Implement dont why explanatory query
description:
Implement 'dont why <entity-id>' as specified in dont-derived-queries. Returns entity plus explanatory context: applicable rules, remediation suggestions, and event history. Returns WhyView payload envelope.

Done when: `cargo test derived::why` passes; 'dont why <id>' emits a WhyView with applicable rules listed; remediation suggestions reference concrete actions; a non-existent entity-id emits a structured not-found error.

title: Implement dont import jsonld adapter
description:
Implement 'dont import jsonld' adapter as specified in dont-import-adapters. Normalise JSON-LD input to dont import relations via shared import infrastructure (dont-3ul). Source-specific normalisation: expand @context before processing; map @id to CURIE using prefix registry; map rdfs:label / skos:prefLabel to term label; map rdfs:comment / skos:definition to definition; reject blank-node subjects (refusal-tier). Unknown predicates: warning-tier, not refusal.

Done when: `cargo test import::jsonld` passes; a well-formed JSON-LD file imports without error; a blank-node-subject file emits a structured refusal.

title: Implement harness-mode detection
description:
Implement harness-mode detection as specified in dont-spawn-protocol. Priority order: --direct > DONT_HARNESS env var > MCP > piped stdout > interactive shell. Deterministic timeout-vs-callback race resolution: the first event (callback or timeout) wins; the second is discarded idempotently.

Done when: `cargo test harness::detection` passes for all five mode paths; DONT_HARNESS env var overrides piped-stdout detection; --direct overrides DONT_HARNESS; race resolution test verifies that a late timeout after a callback produces no duplicate state change.

title: Implement dont import bioregistry adapter
description:
Implement 'dont import bioregistry' adapter as specified in dont-import-adapters. Normalise Bioregistry API responses to dont import relations via shared import infrastructure (dont-3ul). Source-specific normalisation: fetch prefix record from Bioregistry API; map 'name' to term label; map 'description' to definition; map 'prefix' to CURIE prefix; map 'synonyms' to alternate labels; records missing 'name' or 'prefix': refusal-tier; records missing 'description': warning-tier, import with empty definition.

Done when: `cargo test import::bioregistry` passes (using fixture data, not live API); a complete record imports cleanly; a record missing 'prefix' emits a structured refusal.

title: Implement spawn lifecycle: expiry, callbacks, and dont spawns command
description:
Implement spawn lifecycle management as specified in dont-spawn-protocol: spawn expiry with configured timeout window, expiry sweep that emits spawn_timeout event and restores pre-spawn status, and late callback handling that still applies with warning.

AFK path: harness-mode — emit spawn_timeout envelope on expiry. HITL path: direct mode — defer until harness path is verified.

Done when: `cargo test spawn::expiry` and `cargo test spawn::late_callback` pass; a spawned entity times out deterministically and its status reverts.

title: Implement dont import openalex adapter
description:
Implement 'dont import openalex' as specified in dont-import-surface. OpenAlex API adapter with source-specific normalisation and rate limit config. Maps OpenAlex concepts to dont imported_term relations.

Source-specific normalisation: map concept 'id' (OpenAlex URL) to CURIE via openalex: prefix; map 'display_name' to term label; map 'description' to definition when present (warning-tier if absent); map 'ancestors' to dont reference assertions; concepts missing 'id' or 'display_name': refusal-tier.

Done when: `cargo test import::openalex` passes (API fixture); a complete concept imports cleanly; a concept with no description imports with a warning; ancestors are imported as reference assertions.

title: Implement dont import wikidata adapter
description:
Implement 'dont import wikidata' as specified in dont-import-surface. Wikidata SPARQL endpoint adapter with source-specific normalisation. Supports importer-specific rate limit configuration in config.toml.

Source-specific normalisation: query Wikidata SPARQL for item labels and descriptions in English; map item QID to CURIE (wikidata:Q<id>); map rdfs:label to term label; map schema:description to definition; items missing English label: warning-tier; items missing QID: refusal-tier.

Done when: `cargo test import::wikidata` passes (SPARQL fixture); a complete Wikidata item imports cleanly; an item missing English label imports with a warning; rate limit config in config.toml is respected.

title: Implement dont overlook spawn verb
description:
Implement 'dont overlook' spawn verb as specified in dont-spawn-protocol. Emits a spawn_request envelope in harness mode; calls the configured LLM provider in direct mode.

AFK path (harness mode): emit spawn_request envelope with overlook intent — implement and verify this path first.
HITL path (direct mode): call configured LLM provider from config.toml — defer until harness path is verified and LLM provider config (dont-2tl) is in place.

Done when: `cargo test spawn::overlook_harness` passes; harness-mode emits correct envelope; direct-mode path is gated behind --direct flag.

title: Implement dont assume spawn verb
description:
Implement 'dont assume' spawn verb as specified in dont-spawn-protocol. Emits a spawn_request envelope in harness mode; calls the configured LLM provider in direct mode.

AFK path (harness mode): emit spawn_request envelope with assume intent — implement and verify this path first.
HITL path (direct mode): call configured LLM provider from config.toml — defer until harness path is verified and LLM provider config (dont-2tl) is in place.

Done when: `cargo test spawn::assume_harness` passes; harness-mode emits correct envelope; direct-mode path is gated behind --direct flag.

title: Implement dont import ols adapter
description:
Implement 'dont import ols' (OLS — Ontology Lookup Service) adapter as specified in dont-import-surface. HTTP-backed adapter with OLS-specific rate limit config support. Applies source-specific normalisation and shared URL safety checks.

Source-specific normalisation: map OLS term 'iri' to CURIE via prefix registry; map 'label' to term label; map 'description[0]' to definition; map 'synonyms' to alternate labels; map 'is_obsolete: true' to a warning-tier flag; terms missing 'iri' or 'label': refusal-tier.

Done when: `cargo test import::ols` passes (fixture data); a complete OLS term record imports cleanly; a record with is_obsolete: true imports with a warning; a term missing 'iri' emits a structured refusal.

title: Implement dont import obo adapter
description:
Implement 'dont import obo' adapter as specified in dont-import-adapters. Normalise OBO-format input to dont import relations via shared import infrastructure (dont-3ul). Source-specific normalisation: parse OBO stanza headers (id:, name:, def:, synonym:, is_a:, relationship:); map id: to CURIE; map name: to term label; map def: to definition (strip dbxref block); map is_a: and relationship: to dont assertions; reject malformed stanza ids (refusal-tier); unknown tags: warning-tier.

Done when: `cargo test import::obo` passes; a minimal OBO file with id/name/def imports cleanly; a malformed stanza-id file emits a structured refusal.

title: Implement dont guess spawn verb
description:
Implement 'dont guess' spawn verb as specified in dont-spawn-protocol. Emits a spawn_request envelope in harness mode; calls the configured LLM provider in direct mode.

AFK path (harness mode): emit spawn_request envelope with guess intent — implement and verify this path first.
HITL path (direct mode): call configured LLM provider from config.toml — defer until harness path is verified and LLM provider config (dont-2tl) is in place.

Done when: `cargo test spawn::guess_harness` passes; harness-mode emits correct envelope; direct-mode path is gated behind --direct flag.

title: Implement dont rules add and dont rules test
description:
Implement 'dont rules add <file.dl>' for installing project-specific rules (active on next invocation, no restart required) and 'dont rules test <rule-name>' for dry-run evaluation, as specified in dont-rule-cli.

Done when: `cargo test rules::add` and `cargo test rules::test` pass; 'dont rules add my-rule.dl' copies the rule into .dont/rules/ and it fires on subsequent commands; 'dont rules test my-rule' evaluates the rule against the current store without modifying state; an invalid .dl file emits a structured compilation error.

title: Implement dont explain command
description:
Implement 'dont explain <rule-name>' as specified in dont-rule-cli. Returns human-readable explanation of why a rule applies or doesn't apply to a given entity, sourced from the rule's sibling translation.

Done when: `cargo test rules::explain` passes; 'dont explain ungrounded' returns a WhyExplain payload; the explanation references the entity's actual state; an unknown rule name emits a structured not-found error.

title: Implement dont mcp server mode over stdio
description:
Implement 'dont mcp' as specified in dont-mcp-interface. Runs dont as an MCP server over stdio, exposing the same command surface as MCP tools. Envelope-preserving: MCP tool results use the same JSON envelope schema as CLI output. MCP is optional and non-privileged.

Done when: `cargo test mcp::` passes; echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"dont_show","arguments":{"id":"<id>"}},"id":1}' | dont mcp emits a valid JSON-RPC result with the dont envelope; an unknown tool name returns a JSON-RPC error, not a crash.

title: Implement shared import infrastructure
description:
Implement the shared foundation for all import adapters as specified in dont-import-surface: idempotence via deterministic canonical_source_id, shared HTTP rate limiting (4 concurrent, 2 req/s per host, burst of 4), URL scheme safety checks (http/https only, no loopback/private), mixed DNS resolution refusal. Import writes only to import-related relations: imported_term, reference, prefix.

Done when: `cargo test import::shared` passes; importing the same source URL twice inserts no duplicate rows; a private IP URL (192.168.x.x) emits a structured safety refusal; a fifth concurrent request blocks until a slot is free; import writes touch only imported_term, reference, and prefix relations.
notes: Note (SCOPE-003): This is a horizontal prep ticket with no standalone demo value. If the shared infrastructure is small enough, consider folding it into dont-137 (OBO adapter, the first adapter). If kept separate, add an integration test that exercises a minimal import path end-to-end so the issue has a concrete done condition.

title: Implement dont rules list and dont rules show
description:
Implement 'dont rules list' (enumerates active rule catalogue with severities) and 'dont rules show <rule-name>' (shows one rule's details including Datalog source and sibling translation) as specified in dont-rule-cli.

Done when: `cargo test rules::list_show` passes; 'dont rules list' emits a RulesList payload with all active rules and their severities; 'dont rules show ungrounded' emits Datalog source and human-readable translation; an unknown rule name emits a structured not-found error.

title: Implement dont sync-docs managed block rewriting
description:
Implement 'dont sync-docs' as specified in dont-agent-help. Rewrites the managed block in .dont/AGENTS.md and any root-level docs that reference it. Must not edit content outside the managed block markers.

Done when: `cargo test sync_docs::` passes; 'dont sync-docs' updates the managed block in .dont/AGENTS.md; content outside the managed block markers is byte-for-byte identical after the command; a missing managed block emits a structured error rather than creating a partial file.

title: Implement shipped rule: term-nonfunctional-label
description:
Implement the 'term-nonfunctional-label' rule as specified in dont-rule-engine. Warn-severity, off-by-default. Pattern-driven via [rules.term_nonfunctional] config block. Flags labels that don't meet functional naming requirements.

Done when: `cargo test rules::term_nonfunctional_label` passes; rule is inactive unless enabled in config; when enabled, a non-functional label produces a warnings[] entry; a functional label produces no warnings.

title: Implement dont verify-evidence command
description:
Implement 'dont verify-evidence' as specified in dont-lifecycle-verbs. Checks liveness of evidence references without changing entity status. Records per-reference outcomes and warnings. Returns partial results on timeout. Separate from dismiss (deterministic, network-independent).

Done when: `cargo test lifecycle::verify_evidence` passes (using mock HTTP); 'dont verify-evidence <id>' returns a per-reference report; a timed-out check returns partial results without error exit; entity status is unchanged after the command.

title: Implement stdin piping for bulk operations and NDJSON output
description:
Implement stdin piping where dont reads entity IDs line-by-line for bulk operations, and emits NDJSON output in stdin+json mode, as specified in dont-cli-surface.

Done when: `cargo test cli::stdin_pipe` passes; 'echo "id1\nid2" | dont show' processes both IDs; piped output in json mode is valid NDJSON (one JSON object per line); interactive mode is unchanged.

title: Implement dont help command with Diataxis structure and topics
description:
Implement dont help command plumbing as specified in dont-agent-help: route 'dont help', 'dont help <cmd>', '<cmd> --help', and 'dont help --topics' to the correct output. Each flag gets its own red→green→refactor cycle.

Done when: `cargo test help::` passes; `dont help` prints topic list; `dont conclude --help` emits command-specific help; `dont help --topics` lists all available topics.

title: Implement shipped rules: lockable, correlated-error, dangling-definition
description:
Implement three shipped rules as specified in dont-rule-engine: 'lockable' (gates the lock operation), 'correlated-error' (flags shared-source evidence), and 'dangling-definition' (blocks unresolved term relations). Implement with correct severity defaults.

Done when: `cargo test rules::lockable`, `cargo test rules::correlated_error`, and `cargo test rules::dangling_definition` all pass; each rule fires correctly on a fixture; each rule is silent on a clean fixture; correlated-error traversal terminates on a cyclic dependency graph.

title: Implement colour output with NO_COLOR and CLICOLOR_FORCE support
description:
Implement terminal colour output honouring NO_COLOR and CLICOLOR_FORCE environment variables as specified in dont-cli-surface. --plain flag disables colour. Default to colour when interactive.

Done when: `cargo test cli::colour` passes; output with NO_COLOR=1 contains no ANSI escape codes; output with CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 contains ANSI codes even when piped; 'dont list --plain' emits no colour codes.
close_reason: Implemented in baa4c34 (feat(output): make human-readable the default; add ANSI status colors) — NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, --plain flag, and IsTerminal detection all landed as part of OpenSpec 2.1/2.2 work

title: Implement dont ignore lifecycle verb
description:
Implement 'dont ignore' as specified in dont-lifecycle-verbs. Moves eligible entities to ignored state. Requires a substantive reason string. Refuses hedge-only reasons and locked entities.

Done when: `cargo test lifecycle::ignore` passes; 'dont ignore <id> --reason="<substantive>"' transitions entity to ignored; a hedge-only reason ('maybe', 'perhaps') emits a structured refusal; a locked entity emits a structured refusal.

title: Implement shipped rule: stale-cascade
description:
Implement the 'stale-cascade' rule as specified in dont-rule-engine. Computes the stale derived assessment for entities with doubted dependencies. Must be cycle-safe (no infinite loops on circular depends_on). Does not persist status — derived on demand only.

Done when: `cargo test rules::stale_cascade` passes; an entity whose dependency is doubted derives 'stale' assessment; an entity with no doubted dependencies is clean; evaluation on a circular depends_on graph terminates without hanging or panicking.

title: Implement dont reopen lifecycle verb
description:
Implement 'dont reopen' as specified in dont-lifecycle-verbs. Moves ignored entities back to unverified status. Refuses locked entities and derived assessments — reopening locked entities is out of scope for the current implementation.

Done when: `cargo test lifecycle::reopen` passes; 'dont reopen <id>' transitions an ignored entity to unverified; 'dont reopen <locked-id>' emits a structured refusal.

title: Implement shell completions for bash, zsh, fish, powershell, elvish
description:
Add shell completion generation for bash, zsh, fish, powershell, and elvish as specified in dont-cli-surface. Completions must cover all dont commands and their flags.

Done when: `cargo test completions::` passes; 'dont completions bash' emits a valid bash completion script; the script completes 'dont con<TAB>' to 'dont conclude'; all five shells produce non-empty output.

title: Implement config.toml [import] [verify_evidence] [define.shape] blocks
description:
Parse and apply the [import] block (adapter enablement, endpoints, importer-specific sub-blocks), [verify_evidence] block (concurrency, rate limits, retry limits, timeout), and [define.shape] block (validator toggles, compound_markers extensibility) as specified in dont-project-config.

Done when: `cargo test config::import_verify_shape` passes; a disabled adapter in config causes 'dont import <adapter>' to emit a refusal; verify_evidence concurrency limit is respected; a toggled validator in [define.shape] affects 'dont define --label' behaviour.

title: Implement shipped rules: ungrounded and unresolved-terms

title: [bug] F22: no way to delete a claim — dont ignore only relabels, stray claims accumulate
description:
## Finding
From cositos dogfooding evaluation (sandbox/charly-vibes-tools/dev-tooling-evaluation.md §F22).

`dont` offers no `delete`/`remove`/`retract`/`drop` verb. The nearest alternative is `ignore`, which moves a claim to ignored state but leaves it in the ledger. Typos, test claims, and duplicates accumulate permanently and remain visible in claim inventory.

## Reproduction
```
dont conclude "stray test claim"
dont list  # stray claim appears
# no way to remove it — only:
dont ignore claim:<id> --reason "stray"
dont list  # still there, just relabeled
```

## HITL Gate
**A design decision is required before implementation begins.**
Owner must choose one of:

**(a) CLI path:** Add `dont delete <id>` for claims that have not yet been verified or locked. Attempts to delete a verified/locked claim should fail with a clear error. This is the fuller fix.

**(b) Docs + UX path (smaller scope):** Document `ignore` explicitly as the canonical "never mind" / retract verb. Fix `dont status` counts and `dont export` output to exclude ignored claims so the ledger stays clean. No new CLI verb.

Record the chosen direction as a comment before moving to in-progress.

## Acceptance (path a)
`dont delete claim:<id>` removes an unverified claim from the ledger. Attempting to delete a locked claim returns a clear error. `dont list` no longer shows the deleted claim.

## Acceptance (path b)
`dont status` and `dont export` counts exclude ignored claims. `dont ignore --help` or `dont help` documents `ignore` as the intended retract verb.

## Suggested fix
Path (b) is lower risk and ships faster. Path (a) is the more complete fix. If unsure, default to (b) first.

title: 'dont trust' semantics are counterintuitive — reads as establishing trust, not registering doubt
description: 'dont trust <claim>' is meant to register doubt ('do not trust this claim'). However, users reading the command naturally parse it as an instruction to trust the claim. The double-negative naming convention ('dont' + verb = 'do not' + verb) requires learning a mental translation layer. The command description says 'Read as dont trust = do not trust it' but this disclaimer is easy to miss and the friction remains. Consider renaming the command to something unambiguous like 'doubt' or 'flag-doubt', or at minimum make the semantic inversion more prominent in the help text and onboarding.

title: UX: no way to reverse a 'doubted' state except by verifying
description: Once a claim is marked `doubted` via `dont trust`, the only way to move it is `dont dismiss` (verify) or `dont ignore`. There is no command to return it to `unverified` status. Running `dont reopen` on a doubted claim returns 'cannot reopen a Doubted entity — only ignored entities can be reopened'. If you change your mind about a doubt, you're forced to either verify or ignore.
notes: HITL REQUIRED: This issue describes behavior that the dont-lifecycle-verbs spec explicitly defines: 'reopen refuses non-ignored entities — WHEN an actor invokes reopen on an entity whose persisted status is unverified, verified, or doubted — THEN the command is refused.' title: UX: show accepts term:ID but not CURIE; error says 'claim not found'
description:
